rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: let us think from Black's side, with Black to move. Game RoshanGhaderi × Evgeni_Melnikov, Lichess 2020. The white queen has entered the corner of your camp, on a8.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.e2: A trapped piece is one that has no safe square to go to. The queen on a8 is almost like that: b7 and b8 are defended, a7 and a6 are covered, and only the a-file is still open.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.p: Find the move that attacks the queen and takes away its last way out.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.certo: The rook goes to a5 and attacks the queen. The a-file is now closed, and the queen has no safe square left.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the rook to a5: it attacks the queen and closes the a-file, the last way out.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.err.b5b6.1: The rook captures the pawn on b6, but the a-file is still open for the queen.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.err.b5b6.2: With this move the queen comes down the a-file to a3 and leaves the corner. White keeps the advantage.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.err.b5b6.3: Back to the position: the queen only has the a-file to escape. Attack it in a way that closes that exit.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.err.e6e2.1: The rook attacks the bishop on d2, but the a-file is still open for the queen.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.err.e6e2.2: With this move the queen escapes down the a-file to a4 and also attacks your rook on b5.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.err.e6e2.3: Back to the position: the queen only has the a-file to escape. Attack it in a way that closes that exit.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.fora: That move neither attacks the queen nor closes its way out. Look for the move that does both.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: the queen can still escape down the a-file.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.l1: Now White cannot save the queen: all that is left is to capture the rook.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.l2: The queen captures the rook on a5, to take at least one piece.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.l3: The knight on c6 recaptures the queen. Black gave up the rook and won the queen.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex1.l4: This is a trapped piece: the queen had only one way out, and the rook closed it while attacking. In positions like this, count the piece's escape squares and look for the move that takes away the last one.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: another position from a game, now with White: Game dux66 × OutOfComa, Lichess 2025. The black queen has entered your camp, on a2.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.e2: It can still escape along the a-file. The pawn on b3 and the bishop on b2 are defended by your queen, and the rook on e1 covers b1.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.p: Find the move that attacks the queen and leaves it without a safe square.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.certo: The rook goes to a1 and attacks the queen. On any square of the a-file, it is still attacked by the rook.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the rook to a1: it attacks the queen along the whole a-file.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.e4e5.1: The pawn attacks the pawn on f6, but the queen on a2 still has the a-file open.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.e4e5.2: With this move the queen goes back to a7, out of your camp, and White wins nothing.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.e4e5.3: Back to the position: attack the queen in a way that leaves it nowhere to run.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.c4c5.1: The pawn advances, but the queen on a2 still has the a-file open.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.c4c5.2: With this move the queen goes back to a7, out of your camp, and White wins nothing.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.c4c5.3: Back to the position: attack the queen in a way that leaves it nowhere to run.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.e1d1.1: The rook attacks the bishop on d8, but not the queen, which still has the a-file open.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.e1d1.2: With this move the queen goes back to a7, and the bishop on d8 is still defended by the rook on e8.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.err.e1d1.3: Back to the position: attack the queen in a way that leaves it nowhere to run.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not attack the queen, and it escapes along the a-file. Look for an attack that follows it along the file.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: the queen can still escape along the a-file.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.l1: Black cannot save the queen: on any square of the file, it is still attacked.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.l2: The queen captures the rook on a1, to take at least one piece.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.l3: The bishop recaptures. White gave up the rook and won the queen.
rot.trappedPiece.ideia.ex2.l4: Here the queen had a whole file, but the rook attacked the whole file. In positions like this, see whether the attacking piece also covers the escape squares.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.dama.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, in the Game LoveNewUniverse × Chess-Network, Lichess 2021. The white queen has entered your camp, on f7.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.dama.2: The rook on d8 goes to f8 and attacks the queen. That rook covers the f-file and g8, the one on c8 covers e8, the king covers g6 and h5, and the bishop on e7 and the pawn on g7 are defended.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.dama.3: The queen has no safe square. That is why the white bishop first captures the rook on c8, so that White takes at least a rook.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.dama.4: The rook on f8 captures the queen. Black lost a rook and won the queen.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.dama.5: In positions like this, the trapped piece may still let its side capture something before it falls. Count what they take: here, a rook for the queen still left Black with the advantage.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.muitasCasas.1: Attack: Black again, in the Game Xzode × plot987654, Lichess 2024. The white queen on a4 seems to have many squares.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.muitasCasas.2: The rook on b7 goes to a7 and attacks the queen. The bishop on d4 defends that rook.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.muitasCasas.3: No safe square: the rook on b8 covers the b-file and e8, the black queen covers c4 and c6, and the rook on a7, the a-file and d7. Capturing the bishop on d4 would give up the queen. It captures the rook.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.muitasCasas.4: The bishop recaptures. Black gave up the rook and won the queen.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.muitasCasas.5: In positions like this, look square by square: even with many squares, the piece is trapped if all of them are covered. If it has a defender, remove it first, and then capture the piece.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.excecao.1: Attack: now with White, in the Game Gumar5 × YepNope, Lichess 2019. The black queen has entered h3, near the king. Attacking it with the bishop on e2, going back to f1, looks natural. Is attacking enough here?
rot.trappedPiece.demos.excecao.2: The bishop goes back to f1 and attacks the queen.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.excecao.3: The queen escapes along the diagonal to f5, and the game is level.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.excecao.4: Attacking was not enough: the queen still had the diagonal to f5. Back to the position: the right move attacks the queen and closes that diagonal.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.excecao.5: The bishop goes to g4, defended by the queen on d1, and attacks the queen. Everything is covered: h5 by the bishop, h4 and g3 by the pawns, h6 by the bishop on d2, g2, h2 and f1 by the king and the rook.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.excecao.6: The queen has no safe square and captures the bishop, to take at least one piece.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.excecao.7: Your queen recaptures. White gave up the bishop and won the queen.
rot.trappedPiece.demos.excecao.8: In positions like this, count the escape squares before attacking. If one is left, the piece escapes; the good move attacks and takes that square away at the same time.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.valeAqui.enunci: The black queen has entered g2, in your camp. Attacking it with the rook on h1 looks natural. Does it work here? Play as White.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The rook was not enough: the queen escaped with check on g1. The bishop on f3 attacked it and took away g4 and h1; the rook, the king and the pawns covered the rest. The queen captured the bishop, and your queen recaptured it.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.h1: The rook attacks the queen, but it escapes with check on g1, and the game is level. Look for an attack that leaves it no way out.
The rook leaves the corner, but it does not attack the queen, and the game is level. Look for the move that attacks the queen and leaves it without a safe square.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err.e1: The king goes to d2, but the knight on f6 gives check on e4, and Black wins material. The queen on g2 is almost trapped: attack it.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err2.e: That move leaves the black queen on f3, where it has just captured your bishop. Recapture the queen now.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.valeAqui.err2.h: That move leaves the black queen on f3, where it has just captured your bishop. Recapture the queen now.
That move leaves the black queen on f3, where it has just captured your bishop. Recapture the queen now.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.torre.enunciado: The black rook on a8 is in the corner, behind its own pieces: the knight on b8 and the pawn on a7. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.torre.fim: The rook on a8 already had no square: it only needed to be attacked. The bishop on e4 attacked it along the diagonal, and the knight left b8 too late. You won the rook.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.torre.err.c1f4: The bishop goes to f4, but the rook on a8 is not attacked, and Black has time to free it. Look for the move that attacks the rook.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.torre.err.f3f4: The pawn advances, but the rook on a8 is not attacked, and Black has time to free it. Look for the move that attacks the rook.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.torre.err.a3a4: The pawn advances, but the rook on a8 is not attacked, and Black has time to free it. Look for the move that attacks the rook.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.torre.err2.a3a4: The knight has left b8, and the rook on a8 can now get free along the eighth rank. Capture the rook now, before it gets out.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.torre.err2.c1f4: The knight has left b8, and the rook on a8 can now get free along the eighth rank. Capture the rook now, before it gets out.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.torre.err2.f3f4: The knight has left b8, and the rook on a8 can now get free along the eighth rank. Capture the rook now, before it gets out.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.cavalo.enunciad: Now with Black. The white knight has gone deep into your camp, on e8. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.cavalo.fim: The knight already had no safe square: the rook covered c7, the king covered f6 and g7, and the bishop defended d6. The king attacked it, and it could only leave by capturing the pawn, to fall to the bishop.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.cavalo.err.g7h7: The king moves away, and the knight gets out through f6 with check. The game is level. The knight on e8 has no safe square: attack it.
rot.trappedPiece.pratica.cavalo.err2.f7e: The king gets out of check, but the knight on d6 captures your rook on b7. Capture the knight now.
